title: Recording, mixing: AOS, Why, Why Not, Greenfield Morning I Pushed An Empty Baby Carriage All Over The City by Yoko Ono | 1970
content:
Studio Three, EMI Studios, Abbey Road
Producers: John Lennon, Yoko Ono
Engineers: Phil McDonald, Andy Stephens

A mixing session for Yoko Ono’s debut solo album, Yoko Ono/Plastic Ono Band, took place on 30 October 1970.

On 29 February 1968 she appeared onstage at London’s Royal Albert Hall with jazz musician Ornette Coleman. The music was mostly improvised, based on a set of instructions from Ono. The performers were Ono (vocals), Coleman (trumpet), Charlie Haden (bass), Dr David Izenzon (bass), and Ed Blackwell (drums).

One seven-minute piece, ‘AOS’, recorded during the rehearsal, appeared on Ono’s first solo album Yoko Ono/Plastic Ono Band in 1970. It was mixed on this day.

Ono and John Lennon then mixed her tracks ‘Why’ and ‘Why Not’ for the album.

Also made on this day was ‘Bird FX’, compiled from EMI’s tape effects library. It was edited onto ‘Greenfield Morning I Pushed An Empty Baby Carriage All Over The City’ on 4 November.
